workCoverage.coverageDescription: Covers the July 16, 2026 conversion of four separate Apps Script operational pages into one persistent single-page dashboard embedded in Google Sites. The work included diagnosing iframe navigation failure, preserving the existing backend and JSON response, building unified navigation and a shared view container, integrating Intake, Work Queue, Recommendations, and Completed Work controls, adding refresh and error states, and verifying the complete request lifecycle including acknowledgement and completion emails.

subject.mainFocus: Replacing unstable page-to-page navigation inside a Google Sites iframe with one persistent single-page dashboard that unifies Intake, Work Queue, Recommendations, and Completed Work.
subject.description: Meadows Housekeeping work update for July 16, 2026, documenting the diagnosis, implementation, and end-to-end verification of a single-page embedded operations viewer.

narrative.promptingSituation: The operations interface used four separate Apps Script HTML pages inside a Google Sites embed. The first view change could succeed, but later navigation caused the embedded viewer to disappear.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: Browser-console testing showed that links, destinations, and target behavior were correct, so the failure was not in queue data or action functions. The unstable element was repeated Apps Script page navigation inside a nested Google Sites iframe.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Keep the existing backend while creating one persistent embedded dashboard capable of running the entire housekeeping request lifecycle.
narrative.approach: Replace multi-page HTML routing with a single Dashboard.html response, retain the JSON response option, build one navigation bar and shared view container, connect each view to its existing server functions, and test a real request through every state transition and both automated emails.

progression.title: Diagnosed the disappearing embed
progression.description: Confirmed that links and destinations were correct and isolated the failure to repeated page navigation inside the Google Sites iframe.
progression.result: The problem was reframed as an interface architecture failure rather than a data or action failure.

progression.title: Chose a persistent single-page architecture
progression.description: Preserved the existing Apps Script backend and replaced page-to-page navigation with one Dashboard.html shell.
progression.result: The Apps Script frame could remain loaded while internal content changed.

progression.description: Integrated Intake, Work Queue, Recommendations, and Completed Work into one navigation system and shared container.
progression.result: All four operational areas became accessible without changing the web-app URL.

progression.title: Connected lifecycle actions and feedback
progression.description: Added acknowledgement, sorting, start, notes, completion, review, archive, loading, active-state, error, and refresh behavior.
progression.result: The viewer supported real operational work rather than static display.

progression.title: Verified the complete production workflow
progression.description: Processed a new request through acknowledgement, queue sorting, work start, notes, completion, and reporting.
progression.result: The embed remained visible, both emails sent, and the completed record moved correctly.

problemsEncountered.problem: Repeated navigation between separate Apps Script pages caused the Google Sites embedded viewer to disappear.
problemsEncountered.effect: The operational interface became unusable after later view changes even though individual links and functions were valid.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Replaced page-to-page routing with a persistent single-page dashboard that swaps content inside #app-view.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Navigate among separate /exec?view=... Apps Script HTML pages inside the embed.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: Each operational area already existed as a separate page, and direct routing appeared structurally simple.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: Repeated nested web-app navigation inside the Google Sites iframe caused the viewer to disappear.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Correct links and target behavior do not guarantee stability when an embedded application repeatedly rebuilds its own frame.

turningPoints.title: The backend was cleared as the cause
turningPoints.description: Console testing confirmed that the links, destinations, data, and action functions were behaving correctly.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Work shifted from debugging queue logic to redesigning the embedded navigation architecture.

turningPoints.title: Dashboard.html became the persistent shell
turningPoints.description: All operational views were moved into one document with internal content replacement.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: The application became a single-page operations system instead of four embedded pages.

keyDecisions.decision: Preserve the existing Apps Script backend.
keyDecisions.reason: The queue data, server actions, and email functions were already working; the failure was isolated to page navigation.
consequences: The redesign stayed focused on the interface boundary.

keyDecisions.decision: Serve one Dashboard.html page from doGet(e).
keyDecisions.reason: A persistent shell avoids repeated nested Apps Script page loads inside Google Sites.
consequences: Navigation changes only the internal view.

keyDecisions.decision: Refresh the active view after every successful action.
keyDecisions.reason: Users need immediate confirmation that acknowledgement, sorting, notes, completion, review, and archive actions changed the record.
consequences: The dashboard remains synchronized with the latest server state.

narrative.methodEstablished: When an embedded Apps Script application fails during repeated navigation, first separate backend correctness from frame behavior; then preserve working services and replace multi-page iframe navigation with a persistent single-page shell and server-backed view rendering.
narrative.result: The four-page operations interface became one functioning end-to-end housekeeping request-management dashboard that remains visible inside Google Sites.
lessonsLearned: Embedded navigation failures can exist even when links, targets, data, and actions are correct.
A persistent single-page shell is safer than repeated nested web-app navigation.
Existing backend services should not be rewritten when the failure is confined to the interface boundary.
End-to-end verification must include state changes, emails, refresh behavior, and final record placement.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentSummary: The prior interface used separate Apps Script pages for Intake, Work Queue, Recommendations, and Completed Work. Each link loaded a new /exec?view=... page inside Google Sites. The replacement uses one Dashboard.html document, and navigation changes only the content inside the dashboard while the Apps Script frame remains loaded.

sections.title: Problem Identified
sections.contentSummary: The first queue change could load, but later navigation made the embedded viewer disappear. Console testing confirmed that links, destinations, and target=_self behavior were correct. The failure came from repeated Apps Script page navigation inside the Google Sites iframe rather than queue data or action functions. The design decision was to preserve the backend and replace page-to-page navigation with a single-page interface.
